title: Returning in 1919 and working with Duck Ernest and Jack Carey
summary: Miller says on his return in 1919 he played with Duck Ernest and then Jack Carey, who also paraded; they discuss Carey's earlier band affiliations.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, 1919 I came back. Well, I was going right on playing with a fella called Duck Hunter. Did you ever know him? Then Jack Kelly Stoeman was from Duck Hunter. So I worked with Jack for a long time. But Jack didn't have no brass band, but he paraded too. Jack, been in parades too. Was he a member of a regular brass band or a jumper?
Yeah, he was before I came back.
I think he was with the Maple Leaf. Yeah, because he used to talk about that. But I think the Maple Leaf broke up then. I think he was with Henry Allen too.
I need to have a picture of him with Henry Allen. Yeah, I think so.

I've got to think about it. Pretty sure he was. What did Henry Allen get trumped? I know his son, but I didn't ever know him. He hasn't been dead, no. No, I know, but I didn't ever get a chance to see him. I knew he was living when I came here. I was in Algeria and I hardly was ever over there. I never just visited Algeria as much. Were there stuff I can't have a chord thing, but I know what I'm talking about. Da, da, da.
Yeah, them kind of people, they were playing them on the street. I was playing regular dance music in the street.
